title: double free of a tuple the write path had already freed
live_proof: inspection at the 17.0 pin: writetup_heap (src/backend/utils/sort/tuplestore.c:1500) frees the tuple at :1516-1517, after the BufFileWrite calls at :1511-1514 that can throw; dumptuples:1222 calls it in a loop and clears memtupdeleted/memtupcount only afterwards at :1225-1226; tuplestore_clear:428-432 then walks the same range with GetMemoryChunkSpace and pfree. The pre-fix shape is present.
object: a tuple chunk still listed in memtuples[]
lifetime_ender: writetup_heap frees each tuple as it writes it; a throw leaves the already-freed entries inside memtupdeleted..memtupcount for the cleanup walk to free again
shape: double free through a stale array entry

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completes with no capability fault; the case's own PG_DEFECT probe prints twice, so the defective sequence provably executed -- REACHED-SILENT (2026-10-05, plain purecap, revocation=1 every_free=0). A use-after-free between two palloc chunks never crosses a malloc boundary, so there is nothing for a malloc-granular revoker to reclaim.

status: measured on virtual Capstone (virtual-malloc, virtual-pg-pools) and stock CheriBSD (cheribsd-revocation); each arm's verdict_from names its bundle
nested_why: The object comes from PostgreSQL's own memory manager -- a chunk aset.c or slab.c carved out of a block it took from malloc -- so the defect is nested by the allocator that served it.
fault_sites_why: The stale access is the second pfree, so there is no read probe. pfree hands the pointer to SubletRelease (patch 0003), whose first act is to read the chunk header through it, and the pointer was revoked by the first pfree; the read is GetMemoryChunkMethodID's, inlined into SubletRelease or not. Declared 2026-10-11 for the header-parent design, before its first run; the table design declared SubletRelease alone (c41fcbef), and the lifetime adapter faulted in GetMemoryChunkMethodID.
